newsitem.title: INDIA: India to announce new shipping policy in a month.
newsitem.headline: India to announce new shipping policy in a month.

text.p: India said on Wednesday a new shipping policy to be announced within a month's time would boost the privatisation of the sector.
Surface Transport Minister T.G. Venkatraman told reporters the new shipping policy centred on aspects of industry funding and finance.
"The new shipping policy will be announced in a month's time," Venkatraman said. "It will deal with issues of funding and finance."
He said India's ports privatisation policy, announced in October last year, had received a good response, and would improve further after the new policy was announced.
"The new shipping policy will give a boost to privatisation," Venkatraman said after he inaugurated a trade exhibition in Bombay, home to two of India's busiest ports.
But Venkatraman gave no further details of the policy.
India has recently embarked on an aggressive programme to privatise its minor ports, 139 of which have been identified as possible offers for private investors, both domestic and foreign.
The main feature of the programme is build-operate-transfer (BOT) schemes, under which the facility reverts to the federal government after a certain number of years.
During that period, the private investor has the opportunity to recover his initial investment in building the port.
The programme is part of open-market reforms that began in 1991 to tear down the protectionist walls of a decades-old socialist economy.
"For every port we have got enquiries," Venkataraman said. "We are trying to reduce the time taken for approvals."
He said efforts would be made to ensure that the traffic handled by minor ports would not cut into the share of the country's major ports.

"Of a total of 220 million tonnes of cargo handled by Indian ports, the minor ports only handle 20 million tonnes," said Sharad Kale, chairman of the Bombay Port Trust. "So it does not matter much if their share is boosted a little."
